extracted.intended_audience: people seeking guidance on writing grant/program proposals (educators, higher-education staff, nonprofit grantseekers, program administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical, step-by-step how-to guide that takes a proposal idea through preproposal planning, selecting funders, writing each required proposal component, budgeting, evaluation, dissemination, and submission/renewal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mindset: social value and demystification
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the assumptions that there is social value in writing proposals to seek funding and that there is no special mystique about proposal writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach proposal writing as a learnable, practical activity rather than an arcane skill reserved for a few experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preproposal Phase: planning and information collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The planning and information collection which should be accomplished prior to the actual writing of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather background data, assess needs, clarify goals, and do the preparatory research and organizational planning before drafting the proposal narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Generating and shaping initial proposal ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify promising project concepts, match ideas to organizational capacity and community needs, and refine concepts into fundable project proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing Your Capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluating whether you/your organization can carry out the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess staff expertise, administrative infrastructure, fiscal capacity, and prior experience to determine feasibility and fit with the proposed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing the Idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Turning an initial idea into a developed project plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define objectives, anticipated outcomes, target populations, timelines, and concrete activities that operationalize the idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting the Funding Source
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding and choosing appropriate funders for the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match project goals and eligibility to funder priorities, understand funding mechanisms (federal, state, private), and prioritize funders most likely to support the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual composition of the proposal narrative and materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize content clearly, follow funder instructions, present a logical argument for the project, and craft compelling prose that addresses required sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title Pages, Abstracts, and Accompanying Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing front matter and all required administrative forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create concise title pages and abstracts that summarize the project; ensure all application forms are accurately completed and submitted with the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulating the purpose and goals of the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state project aims, rationale, and the significance of the work in relation to needs and funder priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Need
rubrics_metrics.description: Describing and documenting the problem or need the project addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence, data, and context to justify the project; demonstrate the gap the project will fill and why intervention is necessary now.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailing the methods, activities, timelines, and implementation plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present step-by-step procedures, responsible personnel, schedule/milestones, and how activities will lead to the stated objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing how project outcomes and effectiveness will be measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify measurable indicators, data collection methods, analysis plans, and how evaluation findings will inform project improvement and demonstrate impact to funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning how project results and products will be shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe audiences, channels, timelines, and products for sharing findings, and how dissemination will extend project reach or influence practice/policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Documenting the qualifications of personnel and the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide resumes, organizational capacity statements, prior experience, and evidence that the team is capable of implementing the project successfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing a detailed, realistic project budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop line-item budgets that align with project activities, justify costs, comply with funder rules, and demonstrate fiscal responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review, Submission, Notification and Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding the post-writing logistics: review processes, submission procedures, notification, and options for renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow submission instructions and deadlines, anticipate review criteria and timelines, respond to notifications appropriately, and plan for continuation/renewal if applicable.
